article_title: Metacognitive writing strategies, critical thinking skills, and academic writing performance: A structural equation modeling approach
citation: Mark Feng Teng, Mei Yue. (2022). Metacognitive writing strategies, critical thinking skills, and academic writing performance: A structural equation modeling approach. Metacognition and Learning. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11409-022-09328-5
title: W-GCTA: Watson–Glaser Critical Thinking Appraisal used to assess five critical thinking subtests
description: The W-GCTA, developed by Watson and Glaser (1980), was adopted to assess learners' critical thinking skills through text-based exercises. It comprises five subtests totaling 86 items: evaluation of arguments (25 items), recognition of assumptions (16 items), deduction (25 items), inferences (20 items), and interpreting information (24 items). One point is awarded per correct answer. In this study Cronbach's alpha values "for the five sub-scales ranged from 0.792 to 0.865". Factor analytic studies are reported as supporting its construct validity and relationship with academic performance.
requirements: Administered here as a paper-and-pencil test completed within 60 minutes
constraints: Measures application of core critical thinking skills via text sentences; the article cites earlier studies for validity rather than new validation in this sample
target_learning_goals: Critical thinking skills: inference, recognition of assumptions, deduction, interpretation, evaluation of arguments
examples: Completed by the same 644 participants one week before the academic writing test; instructions were in Chinese to ensure comprehension
